picker.title: Choose your Launchpad
picker.intro: Lunchpad asks every MIDI device to identify itself, so the list below only shows Launchpads it can actually drive.
picker.emptyTitle: Plug in a Launchpad and it will appear here on its own.
picker.emptyHint: Supported: Launchpad MK2, X, Mini MK3, Pro MK2, Pro MK3, and the first generation (Launchpad, S, Mini). On Windows, close other apps that may hold the MIDI ports.
picker.virtualTitle: No Launchpad? Use the pads on screen.
picker.virtualHint: Pick a layout. The pads in the window then run your macros with the mouse, and you can switch to a real Launchpad any time.
picker.autoConnectHintSaved: Connects to the {{model}} on “{{port}}” when it is plugged in.
picker.autoConnectHintVirtual: Starts the on-screen {{model}} layout when Lunchpad opens.
picker.autoConnectHintNew: The Launchpad you connect will be remembered and reconnected on start.
picker.manualHint: Pick the model to show and the MIDI ports to use, for a device that does not answer the inquiry or ports with unusual names.

side.previewNote: On-screen pads: clicks run the macros. Connect a real Launchpad from the device list any time.
side.hintEdit: Right-click a pad to add or edit a button.
side.hintDrag: Drag with {{move}} to move a button, with {{copy}} to copy it.
side.pressHint: Press a button on the Launchpad.

settings.title: Settings
settings.autoConnectHint: Reconnects the remembered Launchpad on start and when it is plugged in.
settings.pressFeedbackHint: Pads without a button glow while pressed, so the connection is easy to check.
settings.restoreHint: Restoring brings back the profile as it was before the last change.
settings.legacyHint: In the old app, open the crash screen or Settings → Pages and copy the configuration to a file, then choose it here. Sounds keep their paths; hotkeys, colours and OBS actions carry over.
settings.pttEnable: Hold a key while push-to-talk sections run
settings.pttHint: Macros can wrap actions in “Push-to-talk on / off”. While such a section runs, Lunchpad holds this key combination for you. A mouse button works too: the middle button or the side buttons.
settings.checkKeyboardHint: On macOS, Lunchpad needs the Accessibility permission to press keys. This opens the system prompt if it is missing.
settings.audioDeviceHint: Sounds play here unless an action picks another device.
settings.obsEnableHint: Needs OBS 28 or newer with the WebSocket server enabled (Tools → WebSocket Server Settings).
settings.slobsEnableHint: Streamlabs Desktop accepts connections from this computer while it is running; there is nothing to switch on. For another computer, turn on Remote Control in Streamlabs (Settings → Remote Control) and enter its token.
settings.slobsTokenHint: Only needed when the host is another computer.
settings.slobsStatusLine: Stream {{streaming}} · recording {{recording}} · replay buffer {{replay}} · studio mode {{studio}}
settings.rememberedOnly: Remembered: {{model}} on “{{port}}”. Not connected right now.
settings.virtualDevice: On-screen pads with the {{model}} layout. No hardware connected.
settings.pagesHint: Every page is a full layout for the Launchpad. Click a page to show it, double-click to rename, drag to reorder, or share it as a file.
settings.developerHint: Shows the connection status, device facts, the MIDI monitor and shared variables next to the pads. Off by default so the window is just your pages.
settings.developerMode: Show diagnostics in the main window
settings.windowHint: The same switches live in the tray menu.
settings.stayOnTop: Keep the window above other windows
settings.minimizeToTrayHint: Closing the window hides it; macros keep running and the tray icon brings it back.
settings.runAtStartupHint: Registers Lunchpad as a login item.
settings.startHiddenHint: Lunchpad opens without a window; the tray icon shows it.
settings.pressThresholdHint: On velocity-sensitive pads, a press lighter than this velocity is ignored (model default 25). Lower it if soft presses are missed, raise it if pads trigger too easily.
settings.haEnableHint: Lunchpad talks to Home Assistant over its web API. Create a long-lived access token on your Home Assistant profile page (Security section) and paste it here.
settings.haTokenHint: Profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token. The token is stored in Lunchpad's settings file.
settings.variablesHint: Shared variables are what macros write with “set variable”, plus the level of every fader as fader.<name>. They survive restarts. Fader values of renamed or removed faders are dropped automatically; anything else stays until you remove it here.
settings.builtinsHint: Every macro and description can read these; they cannot be changed. Times follow this computer's clock, and the streaming apps and the device are read at the moment the action runs.
settings.downloadsHint: Files that HTTP request actions saved and reuse while their request is unchanged. Removing them makes every such request run again.
settings.secretsHint: API keys and passwords your macros need. They live in your system's credential store, never in the profile or the settings file, and are not shown again once saved. In an HTTP request's address, headers, login or body, type {{ and pick secret.<name>.
settings.secretsNameHint: Letters, digits, _ and -. Adding a name that exists replaces its value.

pages.label: Pages
pages.removeDefault: The first page cannot be removed
pages.dragHandle: Drag to reorder, or into another list

editor.previewHint: Hold the preview to see the active colour.
editor.tapOnly: This button reports a tap only: the device sends no release, so there are no released or held actions.
editor.label: Label
editor.caption: Caption
editor.imageHint: PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP or SVG up to 2 MB.
editor.descriptionHint: Shown as a tooltip when you hover the pad. Markdown works: **bold**, `code`, lists, and ``` fenced code blocks. {{name}} shows a shared variable's current value.
editor.descriptionPlaceholder: What this button does, and anything worth remembering about it…
editor.activeHint: Shown while the pad is held or its macro is running.
editor.linkHint: Show the active colour while a streaming app is in a state, for example while this button's scene is live. Follows the app, so buttons stay right when you switch in OBS itself.
editor.testHint: Runs the button as it is saved. Save first to test your changes.
editor.noLedHint: This button has no LED, so colours do not apply. The look is only shown on screen.
editor.whiteLedHint: This button has a single white LED: a colour becomes a brightness.

colour.customHint: Any colour; the LED shows the closest it can.
colour.flashingHint: Alternates between the two colours in time with the Launchpad's clock.
colour.orderHint: Greys first, then colours by hue, brightest shade first.
colour.limitedHint: This Launchpad has red and green LEDs only.

notices.inputPermission: Allow Lunchpad under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, then check again.
notices.undoHint: Removed or cleared. Undo brings it back; ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z and ⇧⌘Z / Ctrl+Y work too, and both are in the right-click menu.
notices.missingHint: Buttons with a missing file show a dot; open them and choose the sound again.
notices.outsideTitle_one: {{count}} button on this page has no pad on the {{model}}
notices.outsideTitle_other: {{count}} buttons on this page have no pad on the {{model}}
notices.outsideHint: They are kept and show up again on a Launchpad with a bigger grid; open the list to drag them onto free pads.

crash.title: Something went wrong
crash.intro: The interface hit an unexpected error. You can try to recover, or restart the application. The details below help when reporting the problem.

about.updatesHint: Lunchpad looks for a new release on GitHub when it starts.
about.license: This software is free under the GNU General Public License v3. Anyone who passes it on has to keep the credits and share the source. If you paid money for it, you got ripped off.
about.trademarks: All product and company names are trademarks™ or registered® trademarks of their respective holders. Use of them does not imply any affiliation with or endorsement by them.
about.specs: All specifications are subject to change without notice.
about.novation: Launchpad is a trademark of Focusrite-Novation.
about.communityHint: Get the latest builds and help on Discord.

diagnostics.title: Report
diagnostics.hint: Copy this into a bug report. It lists versions, your system, MIDI ports, audio devices and the integrations, nothing personal beyond device names.

actions.heldHint: Runs once the pad has been held for {{ms}} ms.
actions.tapHint: With held actions set, these wait and run when a shorter press is released, so a tap and a hold do different things.
actions.loopHint: Runs the pressed actions again and again until the button is released.
actions.empty: Nothing happens yet. Add an action.
actions.waitHint: Wait for this action to finish before the next one starts.
actions.notAvailable: Not available in this version yet. The action is kept and will run once the feature ships.

fields.msFromHint: A number, or a {{variable}} expression such as {{heldMs}} or {{wait}}. When it does not come out as a number, the last plain number is used.

switchPage.name: Switch page
switchPage.desc: Show another page on the Launchpad.

setColor.name: Set colour
setColor.desc: Change and remember the colour of this or any other button.

runButton.name: Run another button
runButton.desc: Run the actions of another button as part of this one.

stopAllMacros.name: Stop all macros
stopAllMacros.desc: Stops every running macro, including this one.

stopThisMacro.name: Stop this macro
stopThisMacro.desc: Stops every macro running on this button, including this one.

restartThisMacro.name: Restart this macro
restartThisMacro.desc: Stops older runs of this button so only the newest continues.

pushToTalkStart.name: Push-to-talk on
pushToTalkStart.desc: Holds the push-to-talk key until the matching “off” marker.

pushToTalkEnd.name: Push-to-talk off
pushToTalkEnd.desc: Releases the push-to-talk key held by the “on” marker.

flipFlopStart.name: Flip flop: A
flipFlopStart.desc: Actions up to the B marker run on every other press.

flipFlopMiddle.name: Flip flop: B
flipFlopMiddle.desc: Actions up to the end marker run on the presses in between.

flipFlopEnd.name: Flip flop: end
flipFlopEnd.desc: Everything after this runs on every press.

setSystemVolume.name: System audio
setSystemVolume.desc: Set, nudge or mute the volume of the speakers or the microphone, fixed or from a fader.

obsStudioMode.name: OBS: studio mode
obsStudioMode.desc: Turn studio mode on or off, or transition the preview scene to the program.

slobsSwitchScene.name: Streamlabs: switch scene
slobsSwitchScene.desc: Make a scene live, optionally in another scene collection.

slobsToggleSource.name: Streamlabs: show or hide source
slobsToggleSource.desc: Show or hide a source in a scene.

slobsSetAudio.name: Streamlabs: set audio
slobsSetAudio.desc: Mute or unmute a mixer source and set its fader.

slobsToggleFilter.name: Streamlabs: toggle filter
slobsToggleFilter.desc: Turn a filter of a source on or off.

slobsStream.name: Streamlabs: stream, record, replay
slobsStream.desc: Start, stop or toggle the stream, the recording or the replay buffer.

slobsSaveReplay.name: Streamlabs: save replay
slobsSaveReplay.desc: Save the replay buffer to a file.

slobsStudioMode.name: Streamlabs: studio mode
slobsStudioMode.desc: Turn studio mode on or off, or push the preview scene live.

httpRequest.name: HTTP request
httpRequest.desc: Call a web address with any method, headers, body and login.

setVariable.name: Set variable
setVariable.desc: Remember a value for later actions.

runScript.name: Run script
runScript.desc: Run a small JavaScript snippet that can read and change variables.

ifStart.name: Condition
ifStart.desc: Actions up to “Otherwise” run when the check holds.

ifElse.name: Otherwise
ifElse.desc: Actions up to “End condition” run when the check does not hold.

ifEnd.name: End condition
ifEnd.desc: Everything after this runs either way.

stopAllSounds.name: Stop all sounds
stopAllSounds.desc: Silences every sound Lunchpad is playing.

addToVariable.name: Add to variable
addToVariable.desc: Count up or down: add a number to a variable.

setFader.name: Set fader
setFader.desc: Move a fader to a value, as if its pad had been pressed.

setAudioDevice.name: Switch audio device
setAudioDevice.desc: Make a device the system default, so all sound plays (or records) through it.

homeAssistantTurn.name: Home Assistant: on / off
homeAssistantTurn.desc: Turn any entity on or off, or toggle it.

homeAssistantSetValue.name: Home Assistant: set a value
homeAssistantSetValue.desc: Brightness, colour temperature, cover position, fan speed, volume, a number or a temperature, fixed or from a fader.

homeAssistantCallService.name: Home Assistant: call a service
homeAssistantCallService.desc: Any service of any domain, with JSON data and placeholders.

getWindow.name: Get window
getWindow.desc: Find a program's window, in front or by title, and remember its handle, title, program, position, size and screen in a variable.

setWindow.name: Set window
setWindow.desc: Bring a program's window to the front, minimize, maximize, move or resize it, put it on a screen, or close it.

mouse.name: Mouse sequence
mouse.desc: Move, click, scroll and drag the mouse, step by step.

debug.name: Debug window
debug.desc: Show a window with a text, placeholders filled in; running the action again updates it.

getScreen.name: Get screen
getScreen.desc: Remember a screen's size, position, scale and DPI in a variable.

actions.dragHandle: Drag to reorder, or into another list
actions.heldEmptyHint: Add actions here for a long press. A press longer than {{ms}} ms counts as holding.
actions.tapHintImmediate: These run right away on every press; the held actions come on top after the hold time.
actions.holdWait: Pressed actions wait until it is clear this is a tap
actions.holdWaitHint: Off: the pressed actions run at once and the held actions are added after the hold time.

keys.capturing: Press a key or a mouse button…

sound.velocityHint: On velocity-sensitive pads a soft press plays quieter than a hard one.
sound.usePlaceholderHint: Type {{ to pick the variable that holds the file, e.g. the file an HTTP request saved. Trim and preview are off because the file is only known when the macro runs.

launch.executablePlaceholder: /path/to/program or an app name on the PATH
launch.killOnStop: Stop the program when the macro stops
launch.killOnStopHint: Otherwise it keeps running on its own.

hotkey.restore: Release held keys at the end
hotkey.restoreHint: Keys that are still held when the sequence ends are released.

volume.hint: Sets the chosen device to this level; “System default” follows whatever is the default at the time. With a variable set, its number (0–100) replaces the slider.
volume.adjustHint: Adds the step to the current volume of the chosen device; negative steps turn it down. A variable replaces the step.
volume.muteHint: Mutes the chosen device, “System default” follows whatever is the default at the time. A device without a mute switch (the Mac's microphone, some USB interfaces) is parked at level 0 and brought back on unmute.

fader.name: Name
fader.stripHint: A touch strip runs three lists: when a finger lands on it (with the first value), while it moves (with every value), and when it is let go. The pitch strip springs back to the middle and reports the release itself; the modulation strip counts as let go once it rests for a moment. All three get the level as value, percent, fraction, step, steps and display.
fader.variablesHint: These actions run when the level changes and get it as value, percent, fraction, step, steps and display. A value action added here reads “value”, this fader's own level, no matter what the fader is called; match the action's unit to the fader (a 0–100 fader → %, a −60–0 fader → dB). Macros elsewhere read the level as fader.<name>, or fader.<id> for a fader without a name.
fader.coverHint: Pads inside the fader belong to it: buttons there and colour actions aimed at them are ignored while the fader exists.
fader.overlap: This fader would overlap another fader.
fader.covered_one: {{count}} button lies under this fader and will be hidden.
fader.covered_other: {{count}} buttons lie under this fader and will be hidden.
fader.moveHint: Move the whole fader with Ctrl or ⌘ and drag; it only lands where every pad is free.
fader.displayToggle: Show the level on another scale
fader.displayHint: For example a −100 to 26 dB range shown as 0 to 100 %. The actions still get the real value; the shown one is available as “display”.
fader.runActionsHint: Off: only the level and the LEDs change.
fader.setHint: Writing to fader.<name> with “Set variable” or “Add to variable” moves the fader too, so a button can nudge a level with “Add to variable: fader.mic, −5”.
fader.rangeHint: The first pad is the one the fader starts on; the run continues in its direction. A larger value at the first pad makes the fader count down.
fader.rangeInverted: Counting down: the first pad is the high end, the last pad the low end. Actions and the fader variable get these values.
fader.controlHint: The hardware supplies the value: turning the knob or touching the strip moves this fader over its range and runs its actions, paced to a few times a second while it moves.

obs.notConnected: {{app}} not connected. Names can be typed until it is.

studio.label: Studio mode
studio.hint: “Transition” makes the preview scene the live scene; it needs studio mode to be on.

obs.unitHintObs: Percent is OBS's own volume scale from the advanced audio properties: 100 % is 0 dB. A 0–100 fader fits it directly.
obs.unitHintSlobs: Percent is the position of the mixer fader: 100 % is the top. A 0–100 fader fits it directly.

vars.name: Name
vars.localHint: Only this macro and the buttons it calls
vars.globalHint: Shared by all macros until the app quits
vars.placeholderHint: Type {{ to pick a variable; what Lunchpad provides (velocity, pressure, x, y, the page, date and time) and your own variables are replaced when the action runs.
vars.amountHint: Adds the number to the variable (negative subtracts); a missing or non-numeric variable counts as 0. Shared variables are kept across restarts.
vars.builtinName: Provided by Lunchpad and cannot be changed.

builtins.velocity: How hard the pad was hit, 1 to 127 (127 on models without velocity)
builtins.pressure: Aftertouch while the pad is held, 0 to 127
builtins.x: Column of the pad, 0 at the left
builtins.y: Row of the pad, 0 at the bottom
builtins.pageId: Id of the page the button is on
builtins.pageName: Name of the page the button is on
builtins.caption: The button's caption
builtins.weekday: Day of the week, like Tuesday
builtins.trigger: Which list is running: down, up, hold, fader, faderTouch or faderRelease
builtins.heldMs: Milliseconds the pad has been held; final for the released actions
builtins.random: A fresh number from 0 to 1 every time
builtins.obs.connected: true while OBS Studio is connected
builtins.slobs.connected: true while Streamlabs Desktop is connected
builtins.model: The connected model, like Launchpad X
builtins.virtual: true for the pads on screen
builtins.downloadDir: Where HTTP actions keep downloaded files
builtins.configDir: Where the profile and settings live

http.multipartHint: multipart/form-data: text fields as name=value lines, plus file parts
http.fileBodyHint: Send the bytes of one file as the body
http.guessedType: Content type (guessed from the file when empty)
http.responseTextHint: The body goes into the variable (first 2 KB)
http.responseFile: Save the body as a file
http.responseFileHint: The response is the file, e.g. audio from a text-to-speech service
http.responseBase64Hint: A JSON field holds the file as base64 (a data: URL is fine)
http.responseUrl: Download a URL from a field
http.responseUrlHint: A JSON field holds the address of the file
http.fieldHint: Field in the JSON, e.g. audioContent or data.0.url; empty = the whole body
http.fileNameHint: Kept in the download folder; the extension comes from the response unless you give one. An absolute path is used as it is.
http.reuseHint: Skip the request when a file for the same address, headers, body and login already exists. With a file name of your own, that name alone decides.
http.secretHint: Keep API keys out of the profile: store them under Settings › Secrets and insert them as secret.<name>.

script.hint: vars and globals hold the variables, Lunchpad drives the app, and the last expression (or return) is the result.
script.queued_one: Would run {{count}} action: {{names}} (a test runs none)
script.queued_other: Would run {{count}} actions: {{names}} (a test runs none)

activePage.doc: The page shown right now, { id, name }, or null.

device.doc: The connected device, { model, port, firmware, virtual }, or null.

button.doc: The button running this script, { pageId, x, y, caption }.

switchPage.doc: Shows a page once the script is done.

params.page: A page id or a page name.

runButton.doc: Runs a button's actions once the script is done.

params.options: { page, trigger }: a page id (default: this button's page) and press, release, tap or hold (default: press).

setFader.doc: Moves a fader once the script is done.

params.name: The fader's name, variable key or id.
params.value: A number or a {{placeholder}}, clamped to the fader's range.
params.runActions: Whether the fader's actions run; default true.

stopAllMacros.doc: Stops every macro, this one included; nothing queued after it runs.

run.doc: Queues any action, given as its JSON.

params.action: An action object such as { type: "playSound", file: "…" }; fields left out take their defaults.

log.doc: Writes to the application log and the test output.

params.values: Anything; objects are written as JSON.

branch.hint: Numbers compare as numbers when both sides are numeric; placeholders work in the value.

audioDevice.hint: Changes the system's default device, the one everything plays or records through. Names come from the system; a name that only partly matches still works.

kindHints.brightness: Turns the light on at this brightness. With a variable set, its number (0–100) replaces the slider; a fader named desk is {{fader.desk}}.
kindHints.colorTemperature: Turns the light on at this colour temperature in Kelvin. A variable replaces the slider when it holds a number.
kindHints.position: 0 is closed, 100 is open. A variable replaces the slider when it holds a number.
kindHints.fanSpeed: 0 turns the fan off. A variable replaces the slider when it holds a number.
kindHints.volume: 0–100 %, sent as the player's volume level. A variable replaces the slider when it holds a number.
kindHints.number: Sent as is, in the entity's own unit and range. A variable replaces the field when it holds a number.
kindHints.temperature: Target temperature in the unit Home Assistant uses. A variable replaces the slider when it holds a number.

ha.dataHint: Optional. A JSON object with the service's fields; {{placeholders}} are filled in before it is sent. The entity above is added as entity_id.

outside.title: Out of sight
outside.hint_one: {{count}} button on this page has no pad on the {{model}}. Drag it onto an empty pad to bring it back.
outside.hint_other: {{count}} buttons on this page have no pad on the {{model}}. Drag one onto an empty pad to bring it back.
outside.none: Every button on this page has a pad.

import.title: Check before importing
import.intro: This file was made elsewhere. Before you run anything from it, read what it does: every finding opens the action in full, and the whole file is listed below. Nothing has been imported yet.

kinds.secret: Uses your secret “{{detail}}”. Its value goes wherever this action sends it, so make sure you trust the destination.
kinds.upload: Uploads a file from this computer: {{detail}}
kinds.insecure: Skips certificate checks for {{detail}}, so anyone on the network could read or alter the exchange.
kinds.login: Carries a login written into the action: {{detail}}
kinds.program: Starts a program on this computer: {{detail}}
kinds.launcher: Opens a launcher or a terminal with {{detail}}. Whatever is typed next runs on this computer, with your rights.
kinds.command: Types what looks like a command or an address: {{detail}}

import.confirm: I have checked these and want to import them.
import.everythingHint: Every page, button and action as it would be imported. Placeholders are marked, secrets in red.

hub.intro: Share buttons, pages and whole configurations with other Lunchpad users, and send things from the hub straight into this app. Everything that arrives is shown to you before it is imported.
hub.signInHint: Opens the hub in your browser, where you sign in with Discord, GitHub or Google and confirm once. The hub gets a token for this app, nothing else: your secrets never leave this computer.
hub.approveHint: Sign in on the page that opened and confirm. This screen updates on its own.
hub.inboxHint: Things sent to this app from the hub. Review them here; nothing runs until you import it.
hub.inboxEmpty: Nothing waiting. Click “Send to Lunchpad” on the hub and it appears here.
hub.fetchHint: A share link (…/s/abcd1234) or a listing address. It lands in the inbox like something sent from the site.
hub.urlHint: Developer mode: another hub, for example one running on this machine. Sign out before changing it.

target.title: Where should it go? The review comes next.
target.padHint: Click a free pad. A pad that already has a button is replaced; pads of a fader are not available.
target.occupied: This pad has a button; it will be replaced.
target.pageHint: The page is added next to your pages. It keeps its name and can be renamed afterwards.
target.profileReplaceHint: Your current pages are replaced. The previous profile can be brought back under Pages & backup → Restore.

errors.noLayout: Connect a Launchpad (or the virtual one) to choose a pad.

hub.waiting: Waiting for you to finish in the browser…
hub.madeWithNewer: needs Lunchpad {{version}} or newer; update the app to import it

share.titleButton: Share this button on the hub
share.titlePage: Share this page on the hub
share.intro: Everyone can find and install it. The hub scans what it does and refuses anything with a written-out token or password; use {{secret.name}} placeholders for those.
share.name: Title
share.summaryHint: What it is for, in a sentence. Shown on the card.
share.descriptionHint: What it needs: OBS running, a secret named so-and-so, a sound file at a path.
share.tagsHint: Up to 8. Enter, comma or space adds one.
share.publicHint: Listed on the hub, found by search.
share.donePublished: Shared. It is live on the hub.
share.donePending: Uploaded. A moderator looks at it before it is listed; only you can see it until then.
share.signInFirst: Sign in to the hub first (Settings → Community hub).
share.titleUpdateButton: Update this button on the hub
share.titleUpdatePage: Update this page on the hub
share.updateIntro: Publishes what is on the pad right now as a new version of “{{title}}”. People who send it to Lunchpad get the newest version.
share.changelogHint: Shown with the version on the hub.
share.doneUpdated: Version {{number}} is live on the hub.
share.doneUpdatePending: Version {{number}} uploaded. A moderator looks at it before it replaces the current one.

backups.title: Configuration backups
backups.hint: Private copies of your whole configuration on the hub: every page with its buttons and faders, nothing else. Only you can see them; the newest 20 are kept. Restoring goes through the same review as an import.
backups.name: Name (optional)

shared.title: Shared from this app
shared.hint: Buttons and pages you shared, and where they live in your pages. Update publishes the current state as a new version.
shared.empty: Nothing shared yet. Right-click a pad, or use the share icon next to a page under Pages & backup.

window.title: Title
window.getHint: {{name}} holds the window as JSON, with {{name}}.handle, {{name}}.title, {{name}}.app, {{name}}.x, {{name}}.y, {{name}}.width, {{name}}.height, {{name}}.screen and {{name}}.minimized beside it. Type {{ref}} as the title of a Set window later to mean that window again.
window.setHint: Picking a window from the list fills in its exact title and program; a remembered window's {{name}} as the title means that window. Screens count from 1; with a screen, X and Y count from its top-left corner, and a blank one keeps the window's place. On macOS this needs the Accessibility permission, Maximize fills the screen, and Send to back hides the program.

mouse.hint: Steps run top to bottom, where the pointer is. Coordinates count from the top-left corner of the main display, or with “relative” from the pointer; a positive scroll goes down or right; a held button stays down until a release step. Placeholders work in every number.
mouse.positionHint: {{name}} holds “x,y”; {{name}}.x and {{name}}.y hold the numbers on their own.

debug.title: Window title
debug.hint: Each Debug window action has a window of its own. It opens on the first run and every later run replaces its text, so a macro can watch its variables change.
debug.onTopHint: The window stays above the other windows, so it is visible while you use the program the macro controls.

screen.hint: {{name}} holds the screen as JSON, with {{name}}.number, {{name}}.x, {{name}}.y, {{name}}.width, {{name}}.height, {{name}}.scale (pixels per point), {{name}}.dpi, {{name}}.primary and {{name}}.count (how many screens there are) beside it.
